method: All 16 vendor pricing pages were independently re-fetched live and compared field-by-field against the previously committed dataset (2026-09-26 version). This ran as a 16-agent parallel workflow, one agent per vendor, each given the vendor's URL and the previously recorded fields, and asked to report matches vs. discrepancies with quoted evidence.

summary.headlineStatBefore: 5 of 16 vendors disclose a separate AI-usage price
summary.headlineStatAfter: 9 of 16 vendors disclose a separate AI-usage price
summary.rootCause: Incomplete original research, not vendor price changes overnight. 4 of the 6 changed rows (Front, HappyFox, Help Scout, Tidio) had real, already-public AI-usage pricing that the original per-vendor research pass simply did not find or report. 1 row (Gorgias) had a range that widened once a previously-unchecked tier was confirmed. 1 row (Zendesk) revealed a new nuance (a named billing mechanism disclosed without its dollar rate) that doesn't change the boolean but changes what is known.

after.unit: per conversation (Autopilot AI agent add-on, a "starting at" rate)

changes.evidence: "Autopilot -- Run complex customer work with our omnichannel AI agent -- Starting at $0.05 /conversation" (front.com/pricing, checked live 2026-09-27)
changes.reason: Missed in original research; the page already disclosed this at the time of original research or shortly before.

changes.evidence: Gorgias's plan comparison table, tier-by-tier automated-interaction rate (gorgias.com/pricing, checked live 2026-09-27)
changes.reason: The Advanced tier's rate was not confirmed in the original pass; the floor of the disclosed range moved down once it was.

changes.evidence: happyfox.com/pricing/, checked live 2026-09-27: "Help Desk Starting at $24/agent/mo", "Chatbot $0.33 per resolution", "Autopilot Pay as low as 2c per successful action"
changes.reason: The original research (2026-09-26) could not reach or parse HappyFox's pricing page and marked the entire record UNKNOWN. Re-checked live and found fully priced, including two separately metered AI products.

after.unit: for the Lyro AI Agent, a separate product (starting price for 50 conversations/month, a bundle rate not a marginal per-conversation price)

changes.evidence: "Lyro AI Agent -- Starts at $32.50/mo. From 50 Lyro AI conversations" (tidio.com/pricing/, checked live 2026-09-27); billing is by conversation volume, not seats
changes.reason: Missed in original research; per-seat status was also newly clarified from unknown to false.

before.note: AI Agents are bundled into Suite Team and above with no separately disclosed per-resolution or per-session price.

after.note: Zendesk now explicitly names and defines a separate AI-usage billing unit ("Automated Resolutions") without publishing its dollar rate -- a materially different finding from 'no separate billing concept at all', even though disclosed stays false since no price is public.

changes.evidence: "Automated Resolutions: ... the unit of measurement used for calculating and billing your account for AI agent usage" (zendesk.com/pricing/, checked live 2026-09-27)
changes.reason: New nuance found; does not change the boolean but materially improves the accuracy of the note.
